title: Nexus Retail - Proactive Runway & Roadmap Tune-up
summary: Quarterly health check focused on runway (cost burn vs committed), latency tail at peak traffic, and next-quarter roadmap for model rollouts. Nexus wants a short pilot for a dedicated pool and a security deep dive before committing to reserved capacity. Finance requested a 2-page TCO comparison and a short summary of mitigation options for cost spikes.
topics: next steps: pricing doc and security intake
action_items: Sofia Patel: Share updated pilot pricing workbook and per-route cost breakdown (due: 2026-11-17)
Ethan Park: Schedule dedicated-pool perf benchmark run with Nexus test harness and share result sheet (due: 2026-11-24)
Maya Chen: Book security deep-dive with Nexus and Redwood Security PM, include SOC2 artifact link (due: 2026-11-19)
Carlos Ramirez: Provide 3 representative peak windows and synthetic traffic script for benchmark (due: 2026-11-16)

next_steps: Send pilot pricing workbook and short TCO one-pager
Run dedicated-pool benchmark using Nexus load script

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Carlos, Priya, Aaron, Tamara, Jae (Nexus)

Summary: quick check-in to triage two cost spikes in Oct, discuss latency tail during peak, and align on pilot scope for dedicated capacity plus security gating items.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're running a bit long so we'll try to keep this focused. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Carlos: Carlos here, Priya, Aaron, Tamara, Jae also on.
[00:18] Sofia: Great, thanks. Maya, Ethan from our side. We flagged a couple items in the pre-read: the Oct usage spikes and the p99.9 tail—we can start there.
[00:30] Priya: Yeah, on Oct 14th we saw a spike where token usage tripled for about 90 minutes; latency shot up and we saw some 5xxs. We were on the hosted tier.
[00:44] Ethan: Right, looking at the logs we saw sustained queueing in the front-end router when concurrency went north of ~350 rps per model. There was also a KV cache miss pattern that amplified compute.
[00:58] Aaron: Interesting - the cache miss bit might be our prefix variance. We did enable conversational context longer than normal for a test.
[01:08] Priya: Yeah, that was the long-context test. But we were surprised the autoscale didn't absorb it gracefully.
[01:18] Ethan: Autoscale did kick but on hosted there was a soft limit and fallbacks to smaller variants happened; that produced higher latency. For guaranteed throughput you can do Dedicated pools which avoid noisy-neighbor scale lag.
[01:32] Tamara: From finance - we need a clear delta: what does Dedicated cost us vs hosted under our burst profile? We want worst-case and median-case scenarios.
[01:46] Sofia: Absolutely. We'll send a one-pager TCO that shows median, 95th, and worst-case per-token and per-hour for your load shapes.
[01:56] Jae: Security question first - is the pilot going to require VPC peering and customer-managed KMS? We need to know for our compliance board.
[02:08] Maya: For Private/On-prem we support KMS integrations and VPC options; for Dedicated we can offer VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS in most cloud regions. We'll put the exact SOC2/HSM artifacts in the security packet.
[02:22] Priya: Can you include the audit log retention settings? Our auditors want 1 year at minimum.
[02:30] Maya: Yes, we'll include retention windows and the export routes (S3, syslog).
[02:40] Carlos: Back to ops - what's the expected latency SLO we could get if we pin a dedicated pool vs hosted with autoscale?
[02:52] Ethan: For models similar to the ones you're using, a medium dedicated pool we've seen stable p99 around 250-350ms and p99.9 in the 500-700ms band under steady state. Hosted p99 can be similar but p99.9 spikes under concurrent bursts because of multi-tenant scale latency.
[03:14] Priya: Are those numbers measured with quantized variants? Some of our throughput gains came from running int8.
[03:22] Ethan: Good call — those bench numbers assume FP16 on A100-equivalent instance types. If you run int8/quantized we can update the table; quantization reduces memory and often lowers p99.
[03:36] Tamara: Pricing - will quantized models be cheaper?
[03:40] Sofia: Yes, typically unit cost drops due to less GPU time; we'll show the delta in the workbook. Also there's a small perf delta in accuracy we'll call out.
[03:52] Aaron: On the cache miss issue, is there an automated prefix cache prewarming we can enable?
[03:58] Ethan: We have prefix KV caching and hints you can set at request time. For your conversational patterns we recommend setting explicit session keys and enabling prewarm for the top 20 routes.
[04:12] Priya: We'll share the top routes after this meeting.
[04:16] Carlos: Ok, timeline - we want a 2-week pilot where you run dedicated pool benchmarks against our traffic. What's realistic?
[04:26] Ethan: Two weeks is fine. We'll need your traffic scripts and sample windows. We'll run baseline hosted vs dedicated with the same model family and a quantized run.
[04:38] Maya: I'll coordinate scheduling and make sure Security is looped in before we start the benchmark.
[04:46] Jae: For the security deep-dive, can you provide the SAML metadata and an example KMS integration doc?
[04:54] Maya: Yep, we'll share SAML metadata and a KMS integration checklist and a short FAQ about key rotation.
[05:02] Tamara: Finance - we will want the pilot cost tracked daily and alerts if daily burn exceeds a threshold.
[05:12] Sofia: We'll instrument cost alerts and share a dashboard. We'll also add token-level drilling per-route.
[05:20] Priya: One more question: how does model fallback work if the dedicated pool runs out of capacity?
[05:28] Ethan: We can define routing rules: failover to a compatible hosted variant, or queue with a backoff. We'll propose canary fallback policies in the pilot config.
[05:40] Carlos: Okay, sounds good. Anything else?
[05:44] Tamara: Please add a brief section on contract options: monthly vs annual reserved and what flexibility we have for headroom.
[05:52] Sofia: Will do. Also we'll include an option for burst credits for seasonal peaks.
[06:00] Priya: Great, thanks.
[06:04] Sofia: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send pricing workbook and a one-pager TCO; Ethan will run the benchmark once we get the scripts; Maya will set up the security call and drop SOC2 artifacts; Carlos/Tamara will confirm budget and provide the traffic windows.
[06:20] Carlos: Confirmed. We can aim to have the load scripts by Monday.
[06:28] Sofia: Awesome. Let's tentatively book a 30-minute follow-up for 2026-11-26 to review the benchmark.
[06:36] Aaron: Works for us.
[06:38] Sofia: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[06:44] (meeting ends)
notes: Transcript contains some auto-caption errors (model names and exact latency percentiles approximated). Security materials referenced: https://redwood.example.com/security/nexus-packet (link placeholder). Pricing workbook to be shared via Salesforce link.
